intro.title: Redux Toolkit — createSlice & createAsyncThunk
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches and displays a list of users from a mock API using Redux Toolkit. You will learn how to use createSlice to define a Redux state slice with reducers for managing user data, and createAsyncThunk to handle asynchronous API calls. The main technologies involved are React, Redux Toolkit, and JavaScript's async/await pattern. By the end, you'll understand how to structure async logic and state updates in a modern Redux application.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, managing complex state like user data, API responses, and UI loading states is common in features such as e-commerce dashboards or social media feeds. For instance, when a user views their order history, createSlice handles local state like filters, while createAsyncThunk fetches order data from a server, showing loaders during the request. This pattern ensures predictable state updates and efficient handling of asynchronous operations, making it essential for scalable React apps with dynamic content.

objectives: Implement a Redux Toolkit slice using createSlice to manage synchronous state updates
Configure async thunks with createAsyncThunk to handle API requests
Integrate async thunks into a slice to manage loading, success, and error states
Manipulate state within reducers to update the store based on action payloads
Bind async thunk actions to React components using dispatch hooks
Construct a Redux store with the configured slice and thunk middleware
Render UI components that respond to async state changes (loading, data, errors)

steps.title: Import from '@reduxjs/toolkit'
steps.instruction: Import **createSlice**, **createAsyncThunk**, and **configureStore** from **'@reduxjs/toolkit'** only. (React-Redux imports are the next step.)
steps.hint: Use one `import { … } from '@reduxjs/toolkit'` line. Do not import Provider or hooks yet.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: one package per import step
import { createSlice, createAsyncThunk, configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';

steps.expectedOutcome: Redux Toolkit core functions are imported from '@reduxjs/toolkit'.
successCriteria: createSlice, createAsyncThunk, and configureStore are imported from '@reduxjs/toolkit'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Import only from '@reduxjs/toolkit' in this step: createSlice, createAsyncThunk, and configureStore.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a single import from '@reduxjs/toolkit' with createSlice, createAsyncThunk, and configureStore.

steps.title: Import from 'react-redux'
steps.hint: Add a second import line: `import { Provider, useSelector, useDispatch } from 'react-redux'`.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: React-Redux hooks and Provider
import { Provider, useSelector, useDispatch } from 'react-redux';

successCriteria: Provider, useSelector, and useDispatch are imported from 'react-redux'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add named imports Provider, useSelector, and useDispatch from 'react-redux'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Import Provider, useSelector, and useDispatch from 'react-redux' on a separate line.

steps.title: Create initial state object
steps.instruction: Create an initial state object with properties 'data', 'loading', and 'error' to manage async state in your Redux slice.
steps.hint: Define a JavaScript object with these three properties. Set 'data' to null, 'loading' to false, and 'error' to null initially.
steps.expectedOutcome: An initial state object is defined with the required properties for managing async operations.
successCriteria: The initial state object has properties 'data', 'loading', and 'error' with appropriate initial values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all three properties (data, loading, error) are included with appropriate initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initial state object should have properties 'data', 'loading', and 'error' to manage async state. Try again.

steps.title: Create async thunk with createAsyncThunk
steps.instruction: Create an async thunk named 'fetchUsers' using createAsyncThunk that fetches data from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users'.
steps.hint: Use createAsyncThunk from Redux Toolkit to define an async action. The first argument is the action type string, the second is an async callback that returns the fetched data.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async thunk named 'fetchUsers' is created that will fetch user data from the mock API endpoint.
successCriteria: The fetchUsers async thunk is defined using createAsyncThunk with the correct API endpoint.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your async thunk is named 'fetchUsers' and fetches from the correct URL.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async thunk isn't quite right. Remember to use createAsyncThunk with the API endpoint and return the JSON data.

steps.title: Create slice with createSlice
steps.instruction: Create a slice using createSlice with the name 'usersSlice', the initial state you defined earlier, and an empty reducers object for now.
steps.hint: Use createSlice from '@reduxjs/toolkit' to define your slice. Pass an object with name, initialState, and reducers properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A usersSlice variable is created using createSlice with the correct name, initial state, and empty reducers object.
successCriteria: The slice is created with createSlice, has name 'users', uses the initialState variable, and includes an empty reducers object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using createSlice correctly. Make sure you have the name property set to 'users', the initialState property referencing your initialState object, and an empty reducers object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The slice wasn't created correctly. Remember to use createSlice from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and pass it an object with name, initialState, and reducers properties.

steps.title: Export slice actions and reducer
steps.instruction: Export the slice's actions and reducer from the slice file so they can be used elsewhere.
steps.hint: Use named exports to export the slice's actions and reducer. The actions are available as usersSlice.actions, and the reducer as usersSlice.reducer.
steps.expectedOutcome: The slice's actions and reducer are exported, making them available for use in components and store configuration.
successCriteria: The slice's actions and reducer are exported using named exports or default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but ensure both the actions and reducer are exported correctly. Check the syntax for named exports.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incorrect. Remember to export the slice's actions and reducer so they can be used elsewhere.

steps.title: Configure Redux store
steps.instruction: Create a Redux store using configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and register the usersSlice reducer.
steps.hint: Import configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and create a store object with a reducer property containing your slice reducer.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Redux store is configured with the users slice reducer registered.
successCriteria: configureStore is imported and used to create a store with usersSlice.reducer in the reducer object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've imported configureStore and created a store with the slice reducer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store configuration is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using configureStore with the slice reducer.

steps.title: Wrap app with Provider
steps.instruction: Import the Provider component from 'react-redux' and wrap your main app component with it, passing the store as a prop.
steps.hint: You need to import Provider from 'react-redux' and use it as a wrapper component with a store prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Provider component is imported and used to wrap the app, making the Redux store available to all components.
successCriteria: Provider is imported from 'react-redux' and wraps the main app component with a store prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported Provider from 'react-redux' and used it to wrap your app with the store prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Provider component is not properly set up. Check that you imported Provider and wrapped your app with it, passing the store as a prop.

steps.title: Create component and import hooks
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named UsersList and import the useSelector and useDispatch hooks from 'react-redux'.
steps.hint: Start by importing the hooks, then define the component. The component can return null for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UsersList component is created and the useSelector and useDispatch hooks are imported from 'react-redux'.
successCriteria: The component is named UsersList, the hooks are imported from 'react-redux', and the component returns null or an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported both useSelector and useDispatch from 'react-redux' and created a component named UsersList.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component or imports are missing. Create a functional component named UsersList and import useSelector and useDispatch from 'react-redux'.

steps.title: Access state with useSelector
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use the useSelector hook to access the users, loading, and error properties from your Redux store slice.
steps.hint: Import useSelector from 'react-redux' and call it with a function that returns the slice state properties you need.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the Redux store state through useSelector, allowing you to read the users data, loading status, and error message.
successCriteria: useSelector is imported from 'react-redux' and used to access state.users.users, state.users.loading, and state.users.error properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're accessing the correct slice properties: state.users.users, state.users.loading, and state.users.error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useSelector hook should be used to access the Redux store state. Import it from 'react-redux' and call it with a function that returns the slice state properties.

steps.title: Get dispatch function with useDispatch
steps.instruction: Inside your UsersList component, call the useDispatch hook to get the dispatch function and store it in a variable named 'dispatch'.
steps.hint: Import useDispatch from 'react-redux' if not already imported, then call it inside your component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The dispatch function is available in your component via the 'dispatch' variable, ready to be used to trigger Redux actions.
successCriteria: The useDispatch hook is called and its return value is stored in a variable named 'dispatch' inside the UsersList component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling useDispatch() and storing its return value in a variable named 'dispatch' inside your UsersList component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dispatch function hasn't been properly obtained. Remember to call useDispatch() and store its return value in a variable named 'dispatch' inside your component.

steps.title: Add UI to display state and loading/error
steps.instruction: Inside your UsersList component, add conditional JSX that shows a loading message when loading is true, an error message when error exists, and the users list when data is available.
steps.hint: You can use the state variables you accessed with useSelector to conditionally render different UI elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display appropriate UI based on the current Redux state: loading indicator, error message, or users list.
successCriteria: JSX includes conditional rendering that checks loading and error states and displays appropriate messages or data
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking both loading and error states before displaying the users data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering isn't quite right. Remember to check loading first, then error, then display the users list.

steps.title: Add button to trigger async thunk
steps.instruction: In the UsersList component, add a button element with an onClick handler that dispatches the async thunk action using the dispatch function.
steps.hint: The button should be placed inside the div, after the heading. Use the dispatch function you have access to from the previous step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button that dispatches an action
<button onClick={() => dispatch(fetchUsers())}>Fetch Users</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element is added to the UsersList component that will dispatch the async thunk when clicked.
successCriteria: The button has an onClick handler that dispatches the async thunk action using the dispatch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has an onClick handler that dispatches the async thunk action.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct onClick handler. Review how to dispatch actions in React Redux.
